title.en: Toussaint represented as a military commander
title.zh: 以军事统帅形象表现的杜桑

alt.en: An ink drawing shows a uniformed rider raising a curved sword above a rearing horse, with Toussaint Louverture written below.
alt.zh: 墨笔画中，穿军服的骑手在腾跃的马上举起弯刀，下方写有杜桑·卢维杜尔姓名。

caption.en: Claude Louis Desrais, Toussaint Louverture on Horseback, about 1802; ink and wash, Met 2022.419. Historical depiction, not a verified likeness.
caption.zh: 克洛德·路易·德雷，《马上的杜桑·卢维杜尔》，约1802年；墨笔淡彩，大都会2022.419。历史描绘，并非已核实的真实容貌。

interpretation.en: The Met identifies this as the model for an 1802 print. Desrais probably never saw Toussaint; the rearing horse uses a European convention for military authority.
interpretation.zh: 大都会将此画识别为1802年版画的底稿。德雷可能从未见过杜桑；腾跃战马采用欧洲表现军事权威的惯例。

title.en: An Almoravid-era silk survives in a Christian shrine
title.zh: 存于基督教圣龛的穆拉比特时代丝织物

alt.en: A worn red and pale-gold textile fragment shows paired winged creatures inside large circular bands, with smaller animals below.
alt.zh: 磨损的红色与浅金色织物残片中，大圆环内有成对带翼动物，下方有较小动物。

caption.en: Textile fragment from the shrine of San Librada in Sigüenza Cathedral, first half of the 12th century; silk and metal-wrapped thread, Met 58.85.1.
caption.zh: 锡古恩萨主教座堂圣利布拉达圣龛织物残片，十二世纪上半叶；丝与包金属线，大都会58.85.1。

interpretation.en: The museum connects these silks to Almería and their likely movement to Sigüenza after the 1147 conquest. That route is an attribution, not a documented itinerary for every fragment.
interpretation.zh: 馆方把这类丝织物与阿尔梅里亚联系起来，认为其可能在1147年征服后流入锡古恩萨。这是归属解释，并非每块残片都有完整流传记录。

title.en: Bolívar remembered in a New York monument
title.zh: 纽约纪念碑中的玻利瓦尔

alt.en: Two adjacent sepia photographs show an equestrian statue on a tall stone pedestal, the rider extending a sword.
alt.zh: 两幅并列的棕褐色照片表现高石座上的骑马雕像，骑手向前伸出剑。

caption.en: Stereograph of R.de la Cora’s Bolívar statue in Central Park, published by Edward and Henry T. Anthony, 1884–1898; Met 2007.457.916. Posthumous commemoration.
caption.zh: 爱德华与亨利·T.安东尼出版，中央公园R.de la Cora玻利瓦尔骑像立体照片，1884—1898年；大都会2007.457.916。身后纪念作品。

interpretation.en: This photograph records a later statue, not Bolívar himself or an independence campaign. The paired views preserve another medium through which his public image circulated.
interpretation.zh: 照片记录的是后来的雕像，并非玻利瓦尔本人或独立战争现场。并列视图保存其公共形象传播的另一种媒介。

title.en: Madero’s victory becomes a printed celebration
title.zh: 马德罗的胜利成为印刷庆典

alt.en: A printed broadsheet headed Gran Marcha Triunfal shows a mounted man surrounded by supporters above two columns of verse.
alt.zh: 题为Gran Marcha Triunfal的单页印刷品上，骑马男子被支持者围绕，下方有两栏诗句。

caption.en: José Guadalupe Posada, broadsheet celebrating Francisco Madero, published by Antonio Vanegas Arroyo, about 1911; Met 46.46.149.
caption.zh: 何塞·瓜达卢佩·波萨达，庆祝弗朗西斯科·马德罗的单页印刷品，安东尼奥·瓦内加斯·阿罗约出版，约1911年；大都会46.46.149。

interpretation.en: The image and verses celebrate Madero’s early success. They communicate a political position rather than a neutral record of all revolutionary demands.
interpretation.zh: 图像与诗句庆祝马德罗的早期胜利，传达一种政治立场，而非中立记录全部革命诉求。

title.en: Zapata’s image in a later impression
title.zh: 后印版画中的萨帕塔形象

alt.en: A black-and-white print portrays a moustached man in a broad sombrero, dark jacket and loose shirt.
alt.zh: 黑白版画表现留胡须的男子，戴宽檐墨西哥帽、穿深色外套与宽松衬衣。

caption.en: José Guadalupe Posada, Emiliano Zapata, design about 1910–1913; later impression printed by José Sanchez, Met 60.678.25.
caption.zh: 何塞·瓜达卢佩·波萨达，《埃米利亚诺·萨帕塔》，设计约1910—1913年；何塞·桑切斯后印，大都会60.678.25。

interpretation.en: The catalog identifies Zapata and dates the design to about 1910–1913. José Sanchez printed this later impression; its exact printing year is unrecorded.
interpretation.zh: 馆录识别人物为萨帕塔，设计年代约为1910—1913年。这张后印本由何塞·桑切斯印制，确切印年未载。

title.en: A quipu makes knotted records tangible
title.zh: 奇普让绳结记录成为可见实物

alt.en: Many brown cords with knots spread downward and outward from a gathered upper cord against a pale display backing.
alt.zh: 多条带结棕色绳索从上方聚拢的主绳向下及向两侧展开，背景为浅色展板。

caption.en: Inka quipu, before 1532; undyed cotton, spun, plied and knotted. Princeton University Art Museum L.2018.4, on loan from Princeton University Library.
caption.zh: 印加奇普，1532年前；本色棉线经纺、合股与打结而成。普林斯顿大学艺术博物馆L.2018.4，借自普林斯顿大学图书馆。

interpretation.en: The surviving cords show the material organization of a record. The object catalog leaves the contents undecoded; the knot values and the information recorded remain unidentified.
interpretation.zh: 存世绳索展示记录的物质组织方式。馆录尚未解读内容，绳结数值及所载信息仍未辨明。
